# Patched bundled SQLite with the existing rusqlite API

Based on the published `rusqlite` 0.37.0 crate, upstream
<https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite>, commit
`44e0ef965580b94d59c5dfe8874b57ab5993a8f7`.
The registry archive SHA-256 is
`165ca6e57b20e1351573e3729b958bc62f0e48025386970b6e4d29e7a7e71f3f`.
The upstream MIT license, source, tests, original manifest, and commit
provenance are retained. The unused package lockfile is omitted; the
application and fuzz workspace lockfiles resolve their dependencies.

The normalized manifest's `libsqlite3-sys` requirement changes from
0.35.0 to 0.39.1. This uses the official registry release,
which bundles SQLite 3.54.1 and fixes
[RUSTSEC-2026-0459](https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db/blob/main/crates/libsqlite3-sys/RUSTSEC-2026-0459.md)
(CVE-2026-119375). No SQLite code is changed, and the package retains its
actual 0.37.0 version.

The optional session module also backports the null-error-message guard
from upstream commit
[9972b1ecf45706ebe2d7b5592f9c9a709e65c896](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/commit/9972b1ecf45706ebe2d7b5592f9c9a709e65c896).
SQLite can return an error from `sqlite3session_diff` without allocating
an error message. `Session::diff` now returns that error with no message
instead of dereferencing a null pointer. The existing `diff` API is retained;
the upstream commit's generic-parameter and unrelated test changes are not included.
Regressions exercise both a denied query with no message and a schema
mismatch with allocated error text. The application and fuzz feature graphs
do not enable this optional module.

The same module backports upstream callback lifetime fix
[01fd57d1dc115c6b5ab0c4b34e330fef7772aa6d](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/commit/01fd57d1dc115c6b5ab0c4b34e330fef7772aa6d).
`Connection::apply` and `apply_strm` now pass a borrowed `ChangesetItem`
to conflict handlers. This optional API change prevents retaining a raw
SQLite iterator after the callback ends. Compile-fail tests cover retaining
an owned item through either API and retaining a borrowed item beyond the
callback lifetime, alongside the normal session application tests.

An ordinary rusqlite 0.41 upgrade is currently blocked: tor-dirmgr 0.47.0
and 0.48.0 require rusqlite below 0.41, while the latest r2d2_sqlite 0.35.0
requires rusqlite 0.40. Keeping the wrapper APIs used by the application
avoids changing those upstream libraries. SQLite's C API supplies the same calls used by
this wrapper. The dependency's Rust minimum is 1.88, below this project's
toolchains.

All application SQLite consumers enable `bundled`; the patched registry
dependency therefore supplies their SQLite implementation on desktop and
mobile. An external `LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG` override still selects
the system library and requires that library to be patched separately.
The unbundled upstream mode now requires SQLite 3.45.3 or newer. SQLCipher
is not enabled by this workspace; this patch makes no claim that an
externally supplied SQLite or SQLCipher is fixed.

Validation uses the existing rusqlite tests with `bundled,hooks,time`, the
optional `session` error handling, application database and EVX state tests,
workspace/mobile feature resolution, and the unchanged security scanner policies. The fuzz
workspace applies the same patch so its SQLite version matches shipping
code. To run the wrapper tests:

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path vendor/rusqlite/Cargo.toml --lib --features bundled,hooks,time,session
cargo test --manifest-path vendor/rusqlite/Cargo.toml --doc --features bundled,hooks,time,session session::
```

The optional session test build also needs libclang and its C headers.
Remove the standalone vendor lockfile generated by that command after
testing. Remove this patch when the Tor and connection-pool dependencies
support an upstream rusqlite release using patched SQLite, after passing
the same compatibility checks.
